recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not change the current Medication value set back to 410942007 or resurrect Medication.package.container for FHIR-7480; any future medication terminology or stale value-set cleanup should be handled as a separate Pharmacy/terminology decision.
issue_request: FHIR-7480 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy correction from the DSTU1 May 2015 ballot. It reported that Medication-related value sets appeared to be the same value set referenced with different names, with the linked MedicationFormalRepresentation value set showing route-of-administration contents instead of the intended medication terminology.
initial_application: Commit 534313123abc479f1c95a22956d9992582f9743c explicitly listed 7480 and changed source/medication/valueset-medication-package-form-codes.xml from SNOMED CT route-of-administration root 284009009 to package-form root 408102007. The companion Medication.code correction was applied by 6ce87fde09500c2d61c86a07ac98f49037e7d747 for FHIR-8064, changing source/medication/valueset-medication-codes.xml from 284009009 to 410942007.
additional_context: FHIR-7480 overlaps the already-audited Medication.code and package/container ballot family: FHIR-7743, FHIR-8022, FHIR-8061, FHIR-8063, FHIR-8064, FHIR-8066, and FHIR-12347. Medication is active in source/fhir.ini. Current Medication.code binds to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/medication-codes, and that value set now composes SNOMED CT is-a 763158003 medicinal product codes because later Published issue FHIR-19294 superseded the 2015 410942007 root. Current Medication no longer has Medication.package.container; package quantity information is represented by Medication.packageSize. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: An empty no-change audit commit was published. No source change is needed because the original route-code problem was applied historically, current Medication.code no longer points at route-of-administration codes, and reapplying the exact 2015 wording would duplicate already-audited companion issues or reverse later final Pharmacy terminology decisions.
